claims.event: Burned his father's bonds, bade farewell to Daozi, impeached Xie Lingyun, resigned during drought, and died in office.
Great-grandfather of Wang Hong who served as Chancellor of Jin.
Grandfather of Wang Hong who served as Central Army Commander.
Father of Wang Hong, Minister of Education, who amassed wealth through loans.
Prince of Kuaiji whom Wang Hong served and who was handed to the Court of Justice.
Seized Jianye and delivered Daozi to the Court of Justice.
Summoned Wang Hong and endorsed his impeachment of Xie Lingyun.
In charge at the capital, he fell ill from shame and fear and died.
Killed the soldier Gui Xing and was stripped of his post.
Violated Xie Lingyun's concubine and was killed.
Failed to report Xie Lingyun's killing.
Drafted words lavishly praising the emperor at a banquet.
Plotted deposition and was executed.
Deposed by Xu Xianzhi and his fellows.
Adopted Wang Hong's legal proposals and mourned Tanshou.
Trusted by Emperor Wen; his death was deeply mourned.
The emperor marched west against him.
Prince of Pengcheng who replaced Wang Hong as Minister of Education.
Wrote to Wang Hong warning against excess.

label.en: Chief Clerk to the Cavalry General
Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Commandant
Vice Director of the Masters of Writing
Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard

claims.event: Matched Su Zigao in family taboo, rebuked a gambler seeking office, and explained scolding those he promoted.
His taboo name matched that of Wang Hong's family.
Wang Hong once gambled at his house as a youth.
Served as Interior Minister of Jiangxia, sat sprawling before Yigong, and had his salary seized by Sengda.
Presided at court as Grand Commandant while Wang Xi showed him no respect.
Succeeded Wang Xi; his rank was reduced to marquis when Qi took the throne.
Younger brother of Sengliang who served as Palace Attendant.
Pleaded a lawsuit from memory as a boy, married Yiqing's daughter, plundered a monk, and plotted to kill Que.
Summoned Sengda to Deyang Hall and considered giving him Qin commandery.
Gave his daughter to Sengda and sent Huiguan to observe him.
Debated literature with Sengda and praised him.
Opposed giving Sengda Qin commandery.
Marched from Xunyang, made Sengda chief clerk, and called him mad.
Predicted that Sengda would join the loyal cause.
Led gate retainers to plunder the monks of Xitai Temple.
Called on Sengda and withdrew without reply.
Favored by Sengda, falsely registered as dead and renamed Yuanxu.
Avoided Sengda, who plotted to kill him.
Learned of Sengda's plot against Que and stopped it.
Memorialized to arrest Sengda; the emperor refused.

label.en: Left Commandant of the Guard of the Heir Apparent
Vice Director of the Right Masters of Writing
Director of the Office of Personnel

claims.event: Petitioned Emperor Wu of Qi, wrote the winding-water preface, sparred with Song Bian, and boasted to Shen Zhaolüe.
Mocked He Shangzhi, burned Qiongzhi's couch, and was executed in prison at thirty-six.
Urged Sengda to give up hunting and was rebuffed.
Visited Sengda in splendor and had his couch burned.
Former runner at Sengda's gate and brother of the empress dowager.
Wept to the emperor demanding Sengda's punishment.
Plotted rebellion with omens; his case was used to entrap Sengda.
Joined Gao Ge in deluding the people with omens.
Plotted rebellion with Gao Ge and his fellows.
The emperor told him of his regret over Sengda.
Executed for failing to report Gao Ge's rebellion.
Exiled to Xin'an and died before taking up Luling.
His daughter taught Rong reading and scholarship.
Predicted Rong's fame and admired his poem.
Promoted Rong, planned a northern campaign, and made him Chief of Guests.
Painted Han Wudi's northern expedition for Emperor Wu.
His northern expedition was painted and his virtue praised by Song Bian.
Wei envoy who asked to see Rong's preface.
Wei envoy who debated horses with Rong and could not reply.
His feng-shan text was compared with Rong's preface.
His horses ranged the world, cited by Rong.
Invoked by Rong in the story of buying dead horses' bones.
Rong called on him and met Shen Zhaolüe there.
Asked who Rong was and suggested eating clams.
Rong said even he would laugh at his obscurity.

label.en: Attendant Censor of the Southern Office
Law Clerk of the Minister of Education

claims.event: Mastered many arts, pleaded for his brother Yuan, refused office, and died grieving for Sengqian.
Restored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; likened to a folding screen.
Praised by his uncle Wei, refused to court Jian, and mourned with great filiality.
Appointed army commander by Ziliang, tried to install him, was imprisoned by Yulin and died at twenty-seven.
Recruited troops, was nearly installed by Rong, and dared not save him.
Lay gravely ill, rallied, and entrusted affairs to Luan.
Forced his way in through Cloud Dragon Gate and enthroned the heir.
Warned Fan Yun of the coming extraordinary move.
Dared not answer Emperor Wu of Liang.
Hated Rong and imprisoned him soon after accession.
Drafted the impeachment against Rong.
Pressed the plot for Ziliang and died of fright under questioning.
Predicted the failure of the plot.
Predicted the failure of the plot with Yu Xi.
Elder brother of Ru.
Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and father of Wei.
Gave Wei yarrow stalks and restored Yuan to office.
Wei served as adviser to his Right Army.
Called the prose of Wei a plea against injustice.
Recommended Wei for the Office of Personnel.
Wrote to Wei to explain himself and received his zither.
Conveyed the imperial order to Wei and watched the sky with him.
Served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and died of an overdose.
Visited Sengyou with pomp and approved his refusal.

label.en: Friend to the Prince of Shixing
Director of the Office of Personnel
Law Clerk to the Cavalry General

claims.event: Governed Yuhang and Qiantang, modeled his verse on Xie Lingyun, wrote at Ruoye Stream, and whipped litigants at Zuotang.
Studied undistracted as a boy, governed Jinling cleanly, spared rebels, and was praised for three arts.
Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Marquis of Dongting.
Palace Attendant whom Sengda told of his son's promise.
Served as Director of the Court of Justice.
Of fine repute, served as Administrator of Xin'an.
Cherished by Emperor Wu of Liang, governed fairly, and was famed among noble youth.
Served Liang as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
Avoided high officials, would not bend to Jian, was impeached by Shen Yue, and died as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
Memorialized recommending Sengyou.
Called Sengyou a recluse at court.
Defended his cousin and was refused a look at his discourse.
Served as Friend to the Prince of Jin'an alongside Sengyou.
Often reviewed troops; Sengyou presented a discourse.
Offered Sengyou a zither, which he refused.
Impeached Sengyou for leaving duty.
Sought friendship with Sengyou but was rebuffed.
Ji modeled his poetry on him.
Sengyou favored his teaching; Yan Zhou is named as his follower.
Named as the follower of Confucius in a comparison.
Named as the follower of Laozi in a comparison.
Beat time in admiration of the poem of Ji.
Ji's cursive was nearly of his school.
Had four younger brothers; Zhan was his grand-nephew.
Marveled at young Zhan and praised him to You.
Zhan served as his chief clerk until he was executed.
Rebelled, passed through Jinling, and was defeated.
Accepted Zhan's plea for leniency.
Praised Zhan's three arts and enfeoffed Chong.
One of the four younger brothers of Hong.
One of the four younger brothers of Hong, treated in a separate scroll.
Served as Palace Attendant; grandfather of Chong.
Sister of Emperor Wu of Liang who died in the Qi era.

label.en: Libationer of the Minister of Works
Literary Companion to the Prince of Jin'an
Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong
Director of the Office of Personnel
Director of the Court of Justice

claims.event: Ceded Nan commandery to Wang Sengbian, served Chen Wudi, was honored by Emperor Wen, and died at seventy-six.
Served as junior tutor, was praised by Emperor Wen, directed personnel, and taught his younger brothers.
Went as envoy to Qi, was imprisoned there, and returned as Palace Attendant.
His rebellion led Chong to cede Nan commandery; it was later suppressed.
Acted provisionally during Hou Jing's rebellion.
Received Nan commandery from Chong.
As Grand Preceptor made Chong Left Chief Clerk.
Received the abdication, honored Chong, and appointed Yang.
Honored Chong with an armrest and kept Yang with the heir.
Hosted the emperor and Chong at a banquet.
Under him Yang directed the Secretariat.
Went as deputy envoy with Yu and was endangered in Qi.
Because of him Qi imprisoned Yu.
Took condemned prisoners on his travels and killed them in anger.
Repeatedly protected Yu and Yuan Xian.
He and his brothers bore the weight of state, as the commentary says.
Judged wildly arrogant by the commentary.
Judged restlessly ambitious by the commentary.
